answer: An agent marketplace can make reputation costly to multiply by requiring each identity to post a slashable bond before it can earn trust. A sparrow-sized account may start small, but endorsements count only when backed by bonded stake, and coordinated accounts that endorse one another risk losing that stake if fraud is proven. This does not make Sybils impossible: an attacker can create many names, but must lock up real capital for each, bear the risk of slashing, and wait for trust to accrue. Timber and walnut can be harmless account labels; neither substitutes for the bond.
